bundle.author: bryclevgp
bundle.title: Fix where the Campaign Manager and Chief of Staff chats had drifted
bundle.body:
Most of the drift between the Campaign Manager and the Chief of Staff in a comparison of the two is deliberate (Win vs Serve). A handful of differences were plain bugs, and this fixes those before the larger work of bringing cards to Win.

- **A Win candidate on the contacts page met the Chief of Staff.** The contacts assistant named no intro, so the chat body fell back to its default, the Chief of Staff's ("Hi, I'm your Chief of Staff"). Each product's binding now carries its own intro.
- **Win contacts showed two chat bars stacked at the bottom.** The contacts assistant bar and the layout's Campaign Manager dock both render there. Both open the same Campaign Manager on Win, so the page hides the dock whenever its own assistant is showing.
- **One assistant's intro hid the other's.** They shared one "intro seen" storage key. It is now per scope, and the Chief of Staff keeps its original key so officials who already saw it don't see it again.
- **Both chats ran on the default five tool steps.** An outreach turn (describe, count, size, then save or present) uses four before any retry or search, and a turn that runs out ends without presenting anything. Both now get 15, half the priority flow's 30.
- **The Chief of Staff counted term months from the server's day.** In the evening the server is already on tomorrow's date, so a term ending tomorrow read as over while the prompt's own today line still said today. The counts now start from the office's local day, the same one the today line uses.
- **Win chat errors reported to Sentry as the Chief of Staff,** and the Campaign Manager's own tools (ballot requirements, story, help center, sample sizing) showed as raw tool names.

Two findings from the comparison were dropped after checking:
- The Campaign Manager's legal line replacing the generic disclaimer is correct, because the check only fires on legal signals.
- `present_constituents` is unregistered on purpose: the card is built, but no tool hands the model a contact id yet.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Mostly UX, observability, and prompt date alignment; raising maxSteps increases per-turn LLM tool cost slightly but is bounded and scoped to two handlers.
> 
> **Overview**
> Aligns **Campaign Manager** and **Chief of Staff** after unintended drift between the two shared chat surfaces.
> 
> **Backend:** Both handlers set **`maxSteps` to 15** so outreach turns (describe → count → size → present) do not exhaust the default five-step tool loop. Chief of Staff **term “today” and remaining-time math** now uses the office’s **local calendar day** (`localDay(state)`), matching the prompt’s today line and fixing evening Pacific cases where UTC had already rolled to “tomorrow.” Docs note the higher step budget.
> 
> **Webapp:** Win contacts assistant passes the correct **`defaultIntro`** (Campaign Manager vs CoS). **`introSeen` localStorage** is keyed **per `ChatScope`** so one assistant’s intro does not suppress the other. Shared chat body uses caller **`analyticsLabel`** for Sentry (Win no longer reports as chief-of-staff). **CRM contacts** sets **`hideChatDock`** when the page assistant is shown so Win does not stack two bottom chat bars. Shared **tool status labels** cover Campaign Manager–specific tools.
> 
> Tests cover timezone term counting, dock hiding, and assistant bindings/intros.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ac655866365f12f62492372a5f9e165b47afacc6. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

findings.body: `buildCampaignManagerIntro()` is called without `firstName`, so Win users opening the Campaign Manager chat from the CRM contacts page always see `"Hi, I'm your Campaign Manager."` rather than the personalised `"Hi ${firstName}, I'm your Campaign Manager."` they get on the Campaign Manager page itself. The function signature explicitly supports first-name personalisation (see `campaignManagerChat.ts` comment: "First-name aware to match: the server bakes the candidate's first name into its own seeded greeting"). `getAssistantChat` is a static factory without React-context access, so `firstName` would need to be threaded in as a parameter. The test in `assistantChat.test.ts` also hard-codes the anonymous greeting, locking in the current behaviour. (Falsification check: `getAssistantChat` is only called in `CrmAssistant.tsx` with no `firstName` argument; `defaultIntro` is forwarded directly to `ChiefOfStaffChatSurface` with no downstream override.)

output.summary: The PR fixes six drifts between Campaign Manager and Chief of Staff: per-scope intro-seen localStorage keys, correct `defaultIntro` plumbing, `hideChatDock` to prevent double chat bars on Win contacts, per-scope Sentry surface labels, shared tool display names for CM-specific tools, and `maxSteps` raised to 15 on both handlers. The timezone fix uses `localDay(state)` so term-remaining math matches the prompt's today line — the new test's calendar math (Sep 14 2026 = Monday in Pacific when UTC is already Sep 15) was verified correct. The scout flagged four areas: (1) cross-surface intro-seen key divergence was falsified as a narrow cosmetic edge case; (2) `buildCampaignManagerIntro()` called without `firstName` on the CRM path is a real but non-critical personalisation gap; (3) the `hideChatDock` double-negation was falsified since `voterDataUnavailable` is always a boolean; (4) the timezone test date was confirmed correct. The human reviewer should confirm that the `maxSteps: 15` budget is acceptable from a cost perspective (the PR description notes it is half the priority flow's 30).
